newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end up, boosted by output data and rumours.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end up, boosted by output data and rumours.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended higher on Wednesday due to the release of weak Japanese industrial output data, investor buying, and rumours, traders said.

"My feeling is that the output data is not very strong. June output was a bit stronger than earlier rumours of a four percent fall, but it was still weak," a trader at a city bank's securities unit said.
Traders said the market had already picked up steam by the time the output data came out at 0430 GMT, as it had been boosted by investor buying of cash bonds early in the morning.
Japan's industrial production in June fell a preliminary 3.1 percent from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis, the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI).
Rumours had circulated in the market during morning trade that June figure could show a fall of four percent from the previous month.

Another rumour, that financier George Soros was beefing up his yen bond portfolio while reducing his Tokyo stock holdings, added to the bullish sentiment of the yen debt market across the spectrum, traders said.
The September ended at 126.21, up from the previous day's close of 125.72. Turnover was 44,075 contracts.
There was talk that banks and foreign investors bought long-term cash bonds during the morning session, a trader for another city bank's securities unit said.
There was also talk that foreign investors had bought JGB futures, a trader for a foreign brokerage house said.
Cash bonds were bought further after the close of JGB futures trade, on news that construction firm Tada Corp had filed for court protection, traders said.
The key 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.130 percent as of 0647 GMT, down from Tuesday's close of 2.190 percent.
The JGB market has been supported by concern about construnction firms' financial health, especially after Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd applied for court protection in early July.
Traders say such news sustains a view that a near-term rise interest rates is unlikely and lends support to JGBs.
